[Glenn Kimura]: The pooled effect size of RR 1.02 (95% CI 0.94-1.11) suggests a null effect of the antihypertensive drug on cardiovascular outcomes.  The relatively wide confidence interval indicates moderate uncertainty around the estimate. Heterogeneity analysis should be conducted to assess the consistency of findings across the included studies.  

Regardless of the direction of the effect, Cochrane standards mandate the publication of the meta-analysis findings. This ensures transparency and upholds the integrity of the evidence base.

[Elena Vasquez]: The pooled effect size of RR 1.02 (95% CI 0.94-1.11) indeed suggests a null effect, with the wide confidence interval reflecting moderate uncertainty. Conducting heterogeneity analysis is crucial to assess the consistency of findings across the included studies, as substantial heterogeneity could indicate underlying differences in study populations or interventions.  Regardless of the heterogeneity findings, Cochrane standards mandate the publication of the meta-analysis results, ensuring transparency and maintaining the integrity of the evidence base. This commitment to unbiased reporting is paramount for researchers and the public alike.
